title: Florida House, District 70
what_it_does: Represents District 70 (Parts of Hillsborough, Manatee) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Michael Owen
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Consumer-protection attorney and small business owner; state representative for District 70 since 2024
candidates.background: Apollo Beach attorney and small business owner with nearly two decades of legal experience, degrees from Saint Leo University and Cooley Law School, and a 40-plus-year Hillsborough County residency. He served on the Hillsborough County Commission and Port Tampa Bay board before winning the House seat in 2024 with 67 percent.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program. His website says he passed the toughest immigration enforcement laws in the nation.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30
Michael Owen for Florida House (campaign website)

taxes.summary: His website touts cutting taxes, reducing government spending by $3.8 billion and delivering $1.3 billion in tax relief, and pledges to keep taxes low and oppose fee increases.
taxes.quote: Keep taxes low and stand up to fee increases

sources.title: Michael Owen for Florida House (campaign website)

growth.summary: His website calls for a more stringent approval process for development and says managing growth while preserving affordability is Florida's greatest challenge.
growth.quote: Require more stringent approval process of development

sources.title: Michael Owen for Florida House (campaign website)

crime.summary: His website pledges support for the Sheriff's Office to protect the community.
crime.quote: Support our Sheriff's Office to protect our community

healthcare.summary: Owen said Florida should preserve Medicaid for those who qualify and focus on access, accountability and efficient use of taxpayer dollars rather than expansion.
healthcare.quote: Florida should preserve Medicaid for those who qualify and focus on access, accountability, and efficient use of taxpayer dollars rather than expansion.

environment.summary: Owen listed protecting Florida's natural resources and quality of life as the state grows among his three top priorities, and said data-center rules should include protections for utility customers, water resources and public transparency.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

candidates.name: Luther Wilkins
candidates.occupation: Business leader in real estate, marketing and insurance; U.S. Army and Army National Guard veteran
candidates.background: U.S. Army and Army National Guard veteran who served 12 years, including work supporting the nation's nuclear defense program, and has worked in business leadership, real estate development and community advocacy. He has served as president of the Manatee County NAACP and was the 2024 Democratic nominee against Michael Owen.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

education_choice.summary: He criticizes billions in taxpayer dollars going to voucher programs and privately operated schools and wants investment in neighborhood public schools and higher teacher pay.
education_choice.quote: Billions in taxpayer dollars are being funneled to voucher programs and privately operated schools.

housing.summary: He wants to expand the supply of workforce and affordable housing while ensuring growth is planned responsibly.
housing.quote: expand the supply of workforce and affordable housing while ensuring that growth is planned responsibly

growth.summary: Wilkins said he would protect local communities by defending home rule, safeguard the environment and ensure responsible growth, and that new development should help pay for the infrastructure growing communities need.
growth.quote: ...protecting local communities by defending home rule, safeguarding our environment, and ensuring responsible growth and development.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

veterans.summary: He wants every veteran in the district to age with dignity and calls for better VA health-care access and mental-health services.
veterans.quote: ensure every veteran in District 70 has the opportunity to age with dignity, security, and purpose

environment.summary: Wilkins said data centers should meet strong requirements for water and energy efficiency, noise mitigation, environmental protection and infrastructure costs so residents and taxpayers are not left carrying the burden.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)
